subtopicTitle: Transformation between frames — direction cosine matrices

cards.front: What is the direction cosine matrix $C^{b/a}$?
cards.back: The 3x3 matrix whose (i,j) element is the cosine of the angle between the i-th unit vector of frame b and the j-th unit vector of frame a. It transforms vector components via $\mathbf{v}^b = C^{b/a} \mathbf{v}^a$.

cards.front: State the orthogonality property of any valid DCM $C$.
cards.back: $C^T C = I$ and $\det(C) = +1$ (proper rotation). Columns (and rows) are orthonormal unit vectors.

cards.front: What do the rows of $C^{b/a}$ physically represent?
cards.back: Row i is the expression, in frame-b coordinates, of the i-th unit vector of frame a.

cards.front: Write the elementary DCM for a right-handed rotation by angle $\theta$ about the 3-axis.
Given $C^{b/a}$ and $C^{c/b}$, obtain the composite DCM $C^{c/a}$.
cards.back: $C^{c/a} = C^{c/b} C^{b/a}$ (matrix multiplication order follows the sequence of frames).

cards.front: Transform the inertial-frame velocity $\mathbf{v}^i$ of a rocket into body-frame components using the attitude DCM.
cards.back: $\mathbf{v}^b = C^{b/i} \mathbf{v}^i$. The same DCM rotates any free vector between the two frames.

cards.front: Derive Poisson's kinematic equation relating $\dot{C}^{b/a}$ to the angular-velocity cross-product matrix.
cards.back: Differentiate $C^{b/a} (C^{b/a})^T = I$ and use the definition of angular velocity to obtain $\dot{C}^{b/a} = -[\boldsymbol{\omega}^{b/a}\times] C^{b/a}$.

cards.front: Why does a 3-2-1 Euler-angle sequence become singular at pitch = $\pm 90^\circ$?
cards.back: The first and third rotations align, causing loss of rank in the kinematic matrix that maps Euler rates to $\boldsymbol{\omega}$; gimbal lock occurs.
